_comment: Cache panels this fork has adopted, and how each one's components get their names.
A panel out of scripts/interfaces/ is named inter_<id> with every component com_<n>, so a
script that used it would read if_settext(inter_53:com_21, ...) and nobody could tell what
that was. Adopting one means renaming it and its components and moving the file where the
skill lives. tools/genadopt.py does that, and it derives every name FROM THE PANEL'S OWN
TEXT rather than from a hand-written list - so a component that moves, or a panel that is
not the one we think it is, fails the join instead of quietly renaming the wrong thing.
Each panel: src (the cache file), dst, iface (the new interface name), and rules. A rule
matches components on a field pattern; the pattern's named groups feed the name template.
`order` numbers matches left-to-right by x then y when the template needs an index.
Anything no rule matches keeps its com_<n>, because nothing names it.

panels.what: The furnace's own Smelt window. Eight bars, four counts each.

rules.why: the 32 smelt buttons. Each one says which bar and how many, so the button's own option is the key - and that is also what fixes the column order, which is NOT the order smelting.struct lists the bars in (the panel puts Silver before Steel).
rules.name: smelt_{count}_{bar}

rules.why: the eight bar icons. They all ship as obj_bronze_bar and the server sets the real one, so there is no text on them to join with - they are taken left to right, and a check ties each to the button column at the same x.
rules.name: icon{order}

content._why: Which bar each column is. The KEY is the word in the button's own option text, so this table cannot disagree with the panel - genadopt names the buttons from the same words. Everything else about a bar (level, ores, xp, every message) is read at runtime from the smelting_struct the obj already carries, so there is not a single number here.
content._order_note: This is the PANEL's order, left to right: silver is the third column and steel the fourth. smelting.struct lists them bronze, iron, steel, silver - the other way round. A hand-written list would have swapped them and nothing would have noticed.

panels.what: The tanner's window. Eight cells the server fills; Hide and Cost are placeholder labels.

rules.why: the eight cells. The panel is generic - which hide sits in which cell is the server's choice at runtime - so the cells are numbered, not named after a hide.
rules.name: cell{order}

rules.why: the label that says which hide. Jagex left the word Hide in it as a placeholder; the server overwrites it. A LABEL, never a number - there is no %1 in it.
rules.name: name{order}

rules.why: the label that says what it costs. Same placeholder rule.
rules.name: cost{order}

rules.why: the four buttons per cell. File order inside a cell is All, X, 5, 1 - so 1 is appended last, which makes Tan 1 the left click and the top menu row, which is what the live game does. They are numbered by CELL, not 1..32, because a trigger wants to say which hide it is tanning.
rules.name: tan_{count}_{cell}

content._why: The eight cells the panel draws, filled top-left to bottom-right. Six are tannable in this build; the two snake hides have no obj in pack/obj.pack, so their cells are hidden with if_sethide rather than drawn dead. Both cost constants are named here because Canifis is not a fixed markup on Al Kharid - it is 2/5/45 against 1/3/20 - so the window has to read the pair and pick by npc_type.

panels.what: The furnace's Silver Casting window. Seven products, each with a make state and a you-need-the-mould state.

rules.why: the product slot: a 1x1 inv carrying Make 1 / Make 5 / Make 10, which is the inv_button1..3 shape the Castle Wars ticket exchange already uses. File order is product order, and the products block asserts which product each one is against the cache's own Make text.
rules.name: slot_{product}

rules.why: the layer the slot lives in. This is the state shown when you HAVE the mould; if_sethide picks between it and the need layer, and if_sethide only works on layers.
rules.name: make_{product}

rules.why: the layer shown when you do not have the mould, found by its own you-need text.
rules.name: need_{product}

panels._products_why: THE SEVEN PRODUCTS ARE JAGEX'S OWN, not a reading of the panel's labels. scripts/_unpack/727/all.inv carries silvercast_holysymbol, silvercast_unholysymbol, silvercast_sickle, silvercast_lightning, silvercast_tiara, silvercast_agrith and silvercast_commandrod - seven single-slot inventories, one per slot of this panel, each stocking the product it shows - and all seven already have ids in pack/inv.pack. Nothing in this fork had ever used one. They name the three products the panel's own English does not: the lightning rod is fenk_conductor, the demonic sigil is agrith_sigil and the silvthrill rod is burgh_rod_command1. AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS ROUND SAID THOSE THREE HAD NO OBJ IN THIS BUILD AND WOULD STAY DEAD. That was a negative from a hand-guessed name: it searched for lightning_rod, silvthrill_rod and demonic_sigil_mould, none of which is what any of them is called. All six objs and both extra moulds are in pack/obj.pack.
panels._wired_why: Four of the seven are wired. The other three are quest steps - Creature of Fenkenstrain, In Aid of the Myreque and Shadow of the Storm - with no Crafting level and no Crafting experience anywhere to copy, and inventing either would be writing a number from nowhere. Their moulds are packed but nothing in this build hands one out, so their slots stay on the you-need-the-mould side by themselves. No code makes that happen and none should.

panels.what: The churn window a bucket of milk opens: milk makes all three.

rules.why: one button per product, keyed on its own option.
rules.name: churn_{product}

content._why: Three products, and the three panels ARE the three inputs: milk makes all three, cream makes butter and cheese, butter makes cheese. Level is the product's, whatever it was made from; experience is the pair's. Every figure below is from that product's own OSRS wiki page, fetched 2026-09-21, and the three pages agree with each other.
content._xp_note: Experience is written x10, the way every productexp in this repo is: the wiki's 40.5 is 405.
content._obj_note: pot_of_butter is the cache's block name for the item called 'Pat of butter'. An earlier draft of this round said it was the one product with no id in pack/obj.pack and that the round would take one; it is id 6697 and has been all along - the draft had searched for 'pat_of_butter', which is the item's NAME and not its block name. All three products were already packed and this round adds no obj id at all.

panels.what: The churn window a pot of cream opens: cream makes butter and cheese.
The churn window a pat of butter opens: butter makes cheese only.
